Q: TNS_ADMIN environment variable A:

[MS Windows] + R

type in command: systempropertiesadvanced

[Environment Variables...]

create/add a new system variable "TNS_ADMIN" variable ={full path of the tnsnames.ora file location directory }

-- then most application on your PC can start using the global tnsnames.ora file ---

Q: split string only at one single point A:

Simply do .split(/-(.+)/)

When splitting by -(.+) the matching group (.+) will get you the needed second part in its entirety, since .+ will consume all characters after the first - till the end of line:

const text = "Hello world - This is super - easy and cool";
const parts = text.split(/-(.+)/);

console.log(parts[0]?.trim());      // "Hello world"
console.log(parts[1]?.trim());      // "This is super - easy and cool"

P.S: notice above the use of ?.trim() just to get rid of the string wrapping whitespaces for regex simplicity and demo!.
Alternatively, expand the regex to account for optional whitespaces before and after the separator - with \s?

const text = "Hello world - This is super - easy and cool";
const parts = text.split(/\s?-\s?(.+)/);

console.log(parts[0]);      // "Hello world"
console.log(parts[1]);      // "This is super - easy and cool"

Q: Best way to conver HTML content in to PDF A:

I have used Bhowra.Ink for one of HRMS app our org was working on having 3Million conversions. Pure .NET 8, no native deps, handles modern CSS (Grid, flexbox, SVG), A4 pagination, and margins out of the box.

csharp

byte[] pdf = HtmlConverter.ConvertToBytes(html,
    new ConverterProperties { Title = "Doc" }.SetPageA4().SetMargins(36f));

For printing, just write the bytes to a temp file and hand it to PrintDocument or shell it to the default PDF viewer with /print. Silent printing works fine that way without needing a separate print library.
